content: The next dose of this medication should be taken at the regular scheduled time. Storage Instructions: Store the medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Uses: Phentermine is used in combination with a doctor-approved exercise program, behavioral changes, and a reduced-calorie diet to assist with weight loss. It is prescribed for certain overweight individuals, such as those who are obese or have weight-related medical conditions. The exact mechanism by which this medication aids in weight loss is not fully understood, but it may work by suppressing appetite, increasing energy expenditure, or affecting certain areas of the brain. How to Use: Take this medication orally as directed by your doctor, usually once daily, either one hour before breakfast or one to two hours after breakfast. If necessary, your doctor may adjust your dose to a smaller amount taken up to three times daily. Follow your doctor’s instructions carefully. For sustained-release capsules, the dose is typically taken once daily before breakfast or at least 10 to 14 hours before bedtime. Swallow the capsules whole; do not crush or chew them. If using tablets designed to dissolve in the mouth, take the dose once daily in the morning, with or without food. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Your doctor will adjust the dose to determine the most effective amount for you. Discuss the risks, benefits, and duration of phentermine treatment with your doctor. To achieve the best results, take this medication regularly, exactly as prescribed, and for the duration directed by your doctor. Withdrawal and Dependency: If you suddenly stop using this medication, you may experience withdrawal symptoms such as depression or severe fatigue. To prevent withdrawal, your doctor may gradually reduce your dose. Withdrawal is more likely if you have used phentermine for a long time or in high doses. While this medication helps many individuals, it may sometimes lead to addiction. The risk of addiction is higher if you have a history of substance use disorder (e.g., overuse of or addiction to drugs or alcohol). Do not increase your dose, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer period than prescribed. If the medication stops working effectively after a few weeks, consult your doctor. Do not increase the dose unless directed by your doctor. Side Effects: Common side effects may include dizziness, dry mouth, difficulty sleeping, irritability, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or constipation. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, it can cause serious (and sometimes fatal) lung or heart problems, such as pulmonary hypertension or heart valve issues. The risk of these complications may increase with prolonged use or when combined with other appetite-suppressant drugs or herbal products. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other sympathomimetic amines (e.g., decongestants like pseudoephedrine, stimulants like amphetamine, or appetite suppressants like diethylpropion), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. This medication may cause dizziness, blurred vision, or, in rare cases, drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Avoid alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. If using tablets that dissolve in the mouth, note that they may contain aspartame. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: This medication must not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. It may also pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication should not be used with certain drugs due to the risk of serious interactions. Taking monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors with this medication may result in a severe (possibly fatal) interaction. Avoid taking MAO inhibitors (e.g., isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue, moclobemide, phenelzine, procarbazine, rasagiline, safinamide, selegiline, tranylcypromine) during treatment with this medication. Most MAO inhibitors should also not be taken for two weeks before starting this medication. Check the labels of all your medications (e.g. Caffeine can increase the side effects of this medication. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests (e.g., brain scans for Parkinson’s disease), potentially causing false test results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Notes: Appetite suppressants should not replace a proper diet. Do not share this medication with others. Laboratory and/or medical tests (e.g. Keep all medical and lab appointments. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of the next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose. Take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed.
